subject: Post-call: batch/queue savings anchors & next steps
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@paynode.com>, Elena Ortiz <eortiz@paynode.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 May 2025 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: batch/queue savings anchors & next steps

Thanks again for your time today — quick post-call recap and the concrete next asks so we stay aligned. Short version up front: based on the traffic profile you shared, we estimate 25–40% unit cost reduction from batching + prefix/KV caching without any model quality tradeoffs; the attached workbook has the sensitivity table.

What we heard (pain points)
- Token spend is the dominant line item around your POC (current budget target ~$12k/mo for inference).
- Spiky traffic (auth+fraud checks) causes you to avoid large batching today — you need p95 < 200ms on fraud path.
- Many requests share common prompt prefixes (merchant metadata + user history) — good candidate for prefix caching.

Primary goals
- Keep fraud path latency p95 <= 200ms while lowering token spend.
- Validate a 3–6 week pilot that demonstrates >= 20% cost reduction on production-like traffic.
- Procurement-friendly pricing and an operational MAP to speed decisioning.

Anchors and early modeling (see attached paynode_token_modeling.xlsx for full calc)
- Baseline: 600M tokens/month, avg request 120 tokens (prompt+completion), current vendor blended price equivalent: ~$0.0008/token.
- Redwood estimations (conservative):
  - No batching (real-time config): effective cost ~ $0.00072/token (with our low-latency path).
  - With continuous batching + queueing for non-critical paths: effective cost ~ $0.00045/token.
  - Prefix/KV cache expected reduction: 20–30% prompt tokens on the fraud path for repeated prefixes.
- Example ROI anchor (conservative): 600M tokens * ($0.00072 - $0.00045) = $162,000/yr savings (gross) before considering cache wins and operational offsets.

Proposed pilot structure (high level)
1) 6-week technical pilot (staging -> limited prod traffic): measure p95 latency, cost/unit, cache hit rate.
2) Commitment: $6k pilot budget (waived or credit back on expansion if thresholds met) — we can shape as PO + credit.
3) Success criteria: >= 20% reduction in unit spend or $X/month savings at your production mix; p95 fraud path <= 200ms.

Next asks from your side
- Shared results of your token profile export (daily token counts by route) — Samir mentioned you could share a CSV.
- Confirmation on whether tenant-isolated caching is required (we can enable per-tenant cache keys; important for multi-merchant isolation).
- Procurement lead + desired terms for a small PO (we'll draft a one-page pilot addendum).

I'll attach the modeling and a short ROI deck. Marissa and Rishi are looped for sizing and SLA framing. If it looks good I can send a one-page MAP + draft invoice for your procurement team by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: paynode_token_modeling.xlsx (calc), redwood-ROI-deck.pdf (2 slides), mutual-action-plan.csv

From: Samir Patel <samir@paynode.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Ortiz <eortiz@paynode.com>
Date: Wed, 14 May 2025 17:22:13 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: batch/queue savings anchors & next steps

Thanks Stephanie — appreciate the clear summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- SOC2 / Security: we need SOC 2 Type II and evidence of tenant isolation for caching before we route live fraud traffic into a new vendor. Can you point me to the SOC artifact or a security checklist?
- SLA: 99.9% availability for the inference endpoint and p95 < 200ms for fraud path — are these achievable or do they require a dedicated pool?
- Pilot guardrails: we like the idea of a small PO + credit structure. Two asks: can the cache be configured per-merchant (tenant-isolated) and can we cap the monthly spend automatically if we hit a threshold?

If you can send your MAP and a sample pilot invoice, I'll route to procurement (Elena) and legal. Our ideal timeline is to start the pilot in the next 2–3 weeks (we need supplier onboarding done).

—Samir

Samir — thanks, quick answers and an attached MAP that spells the pilot flow out week-by-week. Highlights below and I included a one-page pilot invoice template in the CSV so procurement can see the line items.

Security / SOC2
- SOC 2 Type II: link to secure share (we'll send via SSO to your security mailbox) — we also included the Redwood security checklist in the MAP.
- Tenant-isolated caching: supported. Cache keys can be scoped per-merchant; we'll enable tenant TTLs and optional encrypted keys.

SLA options
- 99.9% availability and p95 < 200ms on the fraud path are achievable with a small dedicated pool for the fraud route (we call this a "latency-reserved lane").
- Recommendation: reserve a small Dedicated slot for fraud traffic during the pilot and route other non-blocking routes through batching. That lets you test both lat/price tradeoffs.

Pilot economics & MAP (attached mutual-action-plan.csv)
- Duration: 6 weeks (technical + limited prod).
- Pilot PO: $6,000 — we will credit $4,000 back on expansion if success criteria met (so net $2k for pilot ops).
- Success criteria: >=20% unit-cost reduction OR >$8k/month extrapolated save at your production mix, and p95 fraud path <= 200ms.

Proposed immediate next steps
1) You share token-profile CSV and the procurement contact. (Samir, you mentioned CSV availability)
2) We provision latency-reserved lane and enable tenant cache keying (Marissa will set config).
3) Legal/procurement receive one-page pilot addendum + sample invoice (attached).

If you want, Marissa can run a 30–45 min tech workshop this week to confirm instrumentation and traffic routing. Rishi will be your SLA/ops contact.

Thanks — if this aligns I'll send the one-page addendum + a DocuSign link for the pilot PO by EOD.

—Stephanie
